name: Score Generation and Composition
title: Score Generation and Composition
answer: Score generation and composition covers systems that create musical notation, MIDI, or audio stems for film, game, advertising, and concert work. It includes melody harmonization, orchestration, arrangement, and full cue generation from text, picture, or temp tracks. The page sits within music composition and audio engineering, not general music production. It addresses both fully generated scores and human-in-the-loop tools that propose material for a composer to edit.

sections.body: Score generation and composition covers systems that create musical notation, MIDI, or audio stems for film, game, advertising, and concert work. It includes melody harmonization, orchestration, arrangement, and full cue generation from text, picture, or temp tracks. The page sits within music composition and audio engineering, not general music production. It addresses both fully generated scores and human-in-the-loop tools that propose material for a composer to edit.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Most current systems run on cloud GPU clusters or local workstations with a modern graphics card, using transformer or diffusion models trained on large collections of scores, MIDI, and audio. Training data is often tokenized into note events, control codes, or spectrogram patches. Inference can be real time for short phrases or take minutes for a full orchestral cue. Among the 2,000 audio models tracked on this site, a smaller subset is designed specifically for score and notation output rather than raw audio synthesis.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is usually done by prompting a model with a text description, a chord chart, a melody, or a reference video segment, then iterating on the output in a digital audio workstation or notation editor. Some tools generate a piano sketch first and orchestrate it in a second pass, while others produce a full mix directly. Composers often treat the output as a starting point, editing note choices, dynamics, and instrument assignments by hand.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on training data provenance, because many models are trained on copyrighted scores and recordings without clear licenses. The site tracks 92 active intellectual property lawsuits, of which 18 involve AI music services, and those cases may shape whether generated scores can be registered or licensed. A composer should keep records of prompts, edits, and source material, and should check the terms of the tool and any publisher or client contract before delivering a generated cue. This is not legal advice, but it reflects current industry practice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward tighter integration with notation software and video editing timelines, so a composer can generate a cue that matches hit points and then refine it in place. Models are also improving at following orchestration constraints, such as instrument ranges and player counts, and at producing stems that separate cleanly for mixing. In the near term, expect more tools that generate a full score and parts from a rough piano sketch, with the composer retaining control over the final musical decisions.
